Tables.name: Segmentation_Master_Dataset
Tables.description: Physician-level dataset containing aggregated promotional activities, prescription data, and physician attributes for pharmaceutical marketing analytics. It will be used for physician segmentation, targeting strategies, and promotional effectiveness analysis.

columns.name: CARDIZOR_NRX
columns.description: This column indicates New Cardizor prescriptions written by physicians for the target pharmaceutical product during the reporting month. NRx (New Prescriptions) represents first-time prescriptions and indicates product adoption and market penetration. Critical for measuring new patient acquisition and product launch success.

columns.name: CARDIZOR_TRX
columns.description: This column indicates Total Cardizor prescriptions written by physicians for the target pharmaceutical product during the reporting month. TRx (Total Prescriptions) represents the complete prescription volume including new and refill prescriptions. Critical for measuring product performance, market share analysis, and physician prescribing behavior.

columns.name: CITY
columns.description: Physician practice location city for geographic segmentation, territory analysis, and market access planning. Enables regional performance analysis and geographic targeting strategies.

columns.name: COMP_1_NRX
columns.description: This column indicates New prescriptions written by physicians for competitor 1 product during the reporting month. Competitive new prescription data enables analysis of competitive new patient acquisition and market penetration. Critical for understanding competitive dynamics and market share trends.

columns.name: COMP_1_TRX
columns.description: This column indicates Total prescriptions written by physicians for competitor 1 product during the reporting month. Competitive prescription data enables market share analysis and competitive positioning assessment. Critical for understanding competitive landscape and physician prescribing preferences.

columns.name: COMP_2_NRX
columns.description: This column indicates New prescriptions written by physicians for competitor 2 product during the reporting month. Competitive new prescription data enables analysis of competitive new patient acquisition and market penetration. Critical for understanding competitive dynamics and market share trends.

columns.name: COMP_2_TRX
columns.description: This column indicates Total prescriptions written by physicians for competitor 2 product during the reporting month. Competitive prescription data enables market share analysis and competitive positioning assessment. Critical for understanding competitive landscape and physician prescribing preferences.

columns.name: DEEPINTENT_CLICKS
columns.description: This column indicates Aggregate count of DeepIntent advertising clicks generated by physicians across all campaigns during the reporting month. Critical for measuring digital advertising engagement and calculating click-through rates.

columns.name: DEEPINTENT_CLICKS_12451
columns.description: This column indicates the count of clicks generated from DeepIntent campaign ID 12451 during the reporting month. Campaign-specific metrics enable detailed analysis of individual campaign performance and optimization. Critical for measuring campaign effectiveness and calculating click-through rates (CTR) when combined with corresponding impression data.

columns.name: DEEPINTENT_CLICKS_13514
columns.description: This column indicates the count of clicks generated from DeepIntent campaign ID 13514 during the reporting month. Campaign-specific metrics enable detailed analysis of individual campaign performance and optimization. Critical for measuring campaign effectiveness and calculating click-through rates (CTR) when combined with corresponding impression data.

columns.name: DEEPINTENT_CLICKS_14284
columns.description: This column indicates the count of clicks generated from DeepIntent campaign ID 14284 during the reporting month. Campaign-specific metrics enable detailed analysis of individual campaign performance and optimization. Critical for measuring campaign effectiveness and calculating click-through rates (CTR) when combined with corresponding impression data.

columns.name: DEEPINTENT_IMPRESSIONS
columns.description: This column indicates Aggregate count of DeepIntent advertising impressions delivered to physicians across all campaigns during the reporting month.  Critical for measuring digital advertising reach and frequency through healthcare professional targeting.

columns.name: DEEPINTENT_IMPRESSIONS_12451
columns.description: This column indicates the count of impressions delivered through DeepIntent campaign ID 12451 during the reporting month. Campaign-specific impression metrics enable detailed analysis of reach and frequency for individual campaigns. Critical for measuring campaign reach and calculating click-through rates (CTR) when combined with corresponding click data.

columns.name: DEEPINTENT_IMPRESSIONS_13514
columns.description: This column indicated the count of impressions delivered through DeepIntent campaign ID 13514 during the reporting month. Campaign-specific impression metrics enable detailed analysis of reach and frequency for individual campaigns. Critical for measuring campaign reach and calculating click-through rates (CTR) when combined with corresponding click data.

columns.name: DEEPINTENT_IMPRESSIONS_14284
columns.description: This column indicates the count of impressions delivered through DeepIntent campaign ID 14284 during the reporting month. Campaign-specific impression metrics enable detailed analysis of reach and frequency for individual campaigns. Critical for measuring campaign reach and calculating click-through rates (CTR) when combined with corresponding click data.

columns.name: DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS_CLICKS
columns.description: This column indicates Comprehensive roll-up of digital advertising clicks across all digital channels (DeepIntent, Relevate Health, Epocrates display, Medscape exposures) during the reporting month. Provides unified view of total digital promotional engagement. Critical for measuring overall digital marketing effectiveness and calculating cross-channel click-through rates.

columns.name: DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS_IMPRESSIONS
columns.description: This column indicates Comprehensive roll-up of digital advertising impressions across all digital channels (DeepIntent, Relevate Health, Epocrates display, Medscape exposures) during the reporting month. Provides unified view of total digital promotional reach. Critical for measuring overall digital marketing impact and cross-channel reach analysis.

columns.name: DIVISION_NAME
columns.description: This column indicates Organizational hierarchy level above territory for management reporting and strategic planning. Enables division-level performance analysis and supports organizational structure reporting for sales leadership.

columns.name: DMD_CLICKED_ECHO
columns.description: This column indicates the count of link clicks generated from DMD Echo email variant during the reporting month. Echo variant represents one of the email campaign variations used in A/B testing or multi-variant campaigns. Critical for measuring email engagement effectiveness and calculating click-through rates (CTR) when combined with delivered email data.

columns.name: DMD_CLICKED_INITIAL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of link clicks generated from DMD Initial email variant during the reporting month. Initial variant represents the baseline or control email campaign variation used in A/B testing or multi-variant campaigns. Critical for measuring email engagement effectiveness and comparing performance across email variants.

columns.name: DMD_DELIVERED_ECHO
columns.description: This column indicates the count of DMD Echo email variant successfully delivered to physicians during the reporting month. Delivery metrics are fundamental for measuring email campaign reach and calculating engagement rates (open rate, click rate). Critical for measuring email campaign effectiveness and list quality.

columns.name: DMD_DELIVERED_INITIAL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of DMD Initial email variant successfully delivered to physicians during the reporting month. Delivery metrics are fundamental for measuring email campaign reach and calculating engagement rates (open rate, click rate). Critical for measuring email campaign effectiveness and list quality.

columns.name: DMD_EMAILS_CLICKED
columns.description: This column indicates Total count of DMD email link clicks generated by physicians across all variants during the reporting month. DMD (Doctor Marketing Database) is a healthcare email marketing platform. Critical for measuring email engagement effectiveness and calculating overall click-through rates.

columns.name: DMD_EMAILS_DELIVERED
columns.description: This column indicates Total count of DMD emails successfully delivered to physicians across all variants during the reporting month. DMD (Doctor Marketing Database) is a healthcare email marketing platform. Critical for measuring email campaign reach and delivery rates across all email variants.

columns.name: DMD_ENGAGEMENT_PLATFORM_ECHO
columns.description: This column indicates the count of physician interactions with DMD platform content attributable to Echo email variant during the reporting month. Includes content views, interactive elements, and other platform engagements triggered by Echo email campaigns. Critical for measuring comprehensive email campaign effectiveness beyond basic email metrics.

columns.name: DMD_ENGAGEMENT_PLATFORM_INITIAL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of physician interactions with DMD platform content attributable to Initial email variant during the reporting month. Includes content views, interactive elements, and other platform engagements triggered by Initial email campaigns. Critical for measuring comprehensive email campaign effectiveness beyond basic email metrics.

columns.name: DMD_HARD_BOUNCED_ECHO
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of hard bounces (permanent delivery failures) for DMD Echo email variant during the reporting month. Hard bounces indicate invalid email addresses or permanent delivery issues. Critical for email list hygiene, quality assessment, and campaign optimization.

columns.name: DMD_HARD_BOUNCED_INITIAL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of hard bounces (permanent delivery failures) for DMD Initial email variant during the reporting month. Hard bounces indicate invalid email addresses or permanent delivery issues.

columns.name: DMD_OPENED_ECHO
columns.description: This column indicates the count of DMD Echo email variant opens by physicians during the reporting month. Email opens indicate initial engagement and interest in the email content. Critical for measuring email campaign effectiveness and calculating open rates when combined with delivered email data.

columns.name: DMD_OPENED_INITIAL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of DMD Initial email variant opens by physicians during the reporting month. Email opens indicate initial engagement and interest in the email content. Critical for measuring email campaign effectiveness and calculating open rates when combined with delivered email data.

columns.name: DMD_UNSUBSCRIBED_ECHO
columns.description: This column indicates the count of unsubscribes from DMD email communications attributable to Echo email variant during the reporting month. Unsubscribe metrics are critical for measuring email campaign impact on physician preferences and list retention. Important for campaign optimization and compliance with email marketing regulations.

columns.name: DMD_UNSUBSCRIBED_INITIAL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of unsubscribes from DMD email communications attributable to Initial email variant during the reporting month. Unsubscribe metrics are critical for measuring email campaign impact on physician preferences and list retention. Important for campaign optimization and compliance with email marketing regulations.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_DOCALERTS_DELIVERED
columns.description: This column indicates the count of DocAlerts successfully delivered to physicians via Epocrates platform during the reporting month. DocAlerts are targeted medical alerts and notifications sent through the Epocrates medical reference platform.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_DOCALERTS_OPENED
columns.description: This column indicates the count of DocAlerts opened by physicians via Epocrates platform during the reporting month. Email opens indicate initial engagement with medical alerts and notifications.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_HIGH_TRAFFIC_DISPLAY_IMPRESSIONS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of impressions delivered through High-Traffic Display advertising units in Epocrates platform during the reporting month. High-traffic display units are premium advertising placements with high visibility and engagement potential.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_HOME_SCREEN_MESSAGE_CLICKS_102
columns.description: This column indicates the count of clicks on Home Screen Messages with creative code 102 in Epocrates platform during the reporting month. Home screen messages are prominent notifications displayed on the main Epocrates interface.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_HOME_SCREEN_MESSAGE_CLICKS_103
columns.description: This column indicates the count of clicks on Home Screen Messages with creative code 103 in Epocrates platform during the reporting month. Home screen messages are prominent notifications displayed on the main Epocrates interface.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_HOME_SCREEN_MESSAGE_CLICKS_104
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of clicks on Prescribing Information links within Home Screen Messages (creative code 104) in Epocrates platform during the reporting month.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_HOME_SCREEN_MESSAGE_CLICKS_105
columns.description: Count of clicks on Prescribing Information links within Home Screen Messages (creative code 105) in Epocrates platform during the reporting month.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_MONOGRAPH_MESSAGE_CLICKS_102
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of clicks on monograph headline messages with creative code 102 in Epocrates platform during the reporting month. Monograph messages are educational content displayed within drug information sections. Aggregation: sum across physicians and time periods for educational content analysis.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_MONOGRAPH_MESSAGE_CLICKS_103
columns.description: This column indicates the count of clicks on monograph headline messages with creative code 103 in Epocrates platform during the reporting month. Monograph messages are educational content displayed within drug information sections.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_MONOGRAPH_MESSAGE_CLICKS_104
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of clicks on monograph headline messages with creative code 104 in Epocrates platform during the reporting month. Monograph messages are educational content displayed within drug information sections.

columns.name: EPOCRATES_MONOGRAPH_MESSAGE_CLICKS_105
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of clicks on monograph headline messages with creative code 105 in Epocrates platform during the reporting month. Monograph messages are educational content displayed within drug information sections.

columns.name: F2F_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of face-to-face (in-person) sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Face-to-face calls represent the highest engagement level in personal promotion and are critical for building strong physician relationships and delivering detailed product information. Critical for measuring in-person physician engagement and sales force field activity.

columns.name: F2F_P1_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of face-to-face Priority-1 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Represents the highest engagement level for the most important physicians, combining in-person interaction with highest priority targeting. Critical for measuring  physician engagement and resource allocation for high-value targets. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: F2F_P2_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of face-to-face Priority-2 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Represents in-person engagement for medium-priority physicians, balancing relationship building with resource efficiency. Critical for measuring standard physician engagement and face-to-face call allocation. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: F2F_P3_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of face-to-face Priority-3 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Represents in-person engagement for standard-priority physicians, typically for routine follow-up or relationship maintenance. Critical for measuring comprehensive physician coverage and face-to-face call distribution. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: MARKET_NRX
columns.description: This column indicates Total market new prescriptions (target product + competitors) written by physicians during the reporting month. Market NRx represents new patient acquisition across the entire therapeutic market. Critical for understanding market growth, new patient trends, and competitive new prescription dynamics.

columns.name: MARKET_TRX
columns.description: This column indicates Total market prescriptions (target product + competitors) written by physicians during the reporting month. Market TRx represents the complete therapeutic market size and enables market share calculations. Critical for market sizing, share analysis, and understanding total addressable market.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_CARDIZOR_RESPONSE_EMAIL_CLICK
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of link clicks generated for product Cardizor from Medscape brand response email campaigns during the reporting month. Brand response emails are targeted promotional communications sent through the Medscape platform. Critical for measuring email engagement effectiveness and calculating click-through rates (CTR) when combined with delivered email data.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_CARDIZOR_RESPONSE_EMAIL_DELIVERY
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of Cardizor response emails successfully delivered to physicians via Medscape platform during the reporting month. Email delivery metrics are critical for measuring campaign reach and calculating delivery rates.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_CARDIZOR_RESPONSE_EMAIL_OPEN
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of Cardizor response emails opened by physicians via Medscape platform during the reporting month. Email opens indicate initial engagement with promotional content.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_DRUG_MONOGRAPH_LINK_CLICK
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of link clicks within Medscape Drug Monograph content during the reporting month. Drug monographs are comprehensive educational resources about pharmaceutical products.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_DRUG_MONOGRAPH_PARTICIPATION
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of physicians who actively participated in or completed actions within Medscape Drug Monograph content during the reporting month. Participation metrics measure deeper engagement beyond simple views.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_DRUG_MONOGRAPH_VIEW
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of views of Medscape Drug Monograph content during the reporting month. Drug monographs are comprehensive educational resources about pharmaceutical products.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_FAST_FIVE_QUIZ_EMAIL_CLICK
columns.description: This column indicates the Count of link clicks generated from Medscape Fast Five Quiz email campaigns during the reporting month. Fast Five Quiz emails are educational quiz-based promotional communications.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_FAST_FIVE_QUIZ_EMAIL_DELIVERY
columns.description: This column inidicates the Count of Fast Five Quiz emails successfully delivered to physicians via Medscape platform during the reporting month. Educational quiz emails are targeted promotional communications with interactive content.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_FAST_FIVE_QUIZ_EMAIL_OPEN
columns.description: This column indicates Count of Fast Five Quiz emails opened by physicians via Medscape platform during the reporting month. Educational quiz emails contain interactive content designed to engage physicians.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_FAST_FIVE_QUIZ_EXPOSURE
columns.description: This column indicates Count of exposures or impressions to Fast Five Quiz content on Medscape platform during the reporting month. Quiz exposures measure the reach of educational quiz content beyond email campaigns.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_FAST_FIVE_QUIZ_LINK_CLICK
columns.description: This column indicates Count of link clicks within Fast Five Quiz content on Medscape platform (outside of email campaigns) during the reporting month. On-platform quiz clicks measure direct engagement with educational content.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_FAST_FIVE_QUIZ_PARTICIPATION
columns.description: This column indicates Count of physicians who actively participated in Fast Five Quiz content on Medscape platform during the reporting month. Quiz participation measures deeper engagement with educational content beyond simple views.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_FAST_FIVE_QUIZ_QUESTION
columns.description: This column indicates Count of quiz questions answered by physicians in Fast Five Quiz content on Medscape platform during the reporting month. Question completion metrics measure depth of educational engagement and learning progress.

columns.name: MEDSCAPE_FAST_FIVE_QUIZ_VIEW
columns.description: This column indicates Count of views of Fast Five Quiz content on Medscape platform during the reporting month. Quiz views measure initial interest and reach of educational quiz content.

columns.name: MONTH_YEAR
columns.description: This column shows first day of month (YYYY-MM-DD format).

columns.name: OTHER_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of sales calls that do not fit into the standard face-to-face or virtual categories during the reporting month. Includes hybrid calls, group presentations, or other non-standard call types. Critical for capturing all sales force activities of physician engagement.

columns.name: P1_CALL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of Priority-1 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Priority-1 calls represent the highest importance level in the sales force targeting hierarchy, typically reserved for high-value physicians or critical business opportunities. Critical for measuring high-priority physician engagement and sales force resource allocation. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: P2_CALL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of Priority-2 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Priority-2 calls represent medium importance level in the sales force targeting hierarchy, typically for physicians with moderate prescribing potential or strategic value. Critical for measuring medium-priority physician engagement and sales force resource allocation. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: P3_CALL
columns.description: This column indicates the count of Priority-3 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Priority-3 calls represent standard importance level in the sales force targeting hierarchy, typically for physicians with lower prescribing potential or routine follow-up requirements. Critical for measuring standard-priority physician engagement and sales force resource allocation. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: PHYSICIAN_CLIENT_ID
columns.description: Internal/CRM physician identifier provided by client specific. This column will be used when NPIs are missing or masked.

columns.name: PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID
columns.description: US National Provider Identifier (NPI) - the universal join key across all pharmaceutical data sources including sales, promotional, and prescription data. Essential for physician identification and data linkage across systems.

columns.name: PHYSICIAN_PDRP_FLAG
columns.description: This columns indicates physician participation in the AMA Physician Data Restriction Program (PDRP), which restricts the use of personal information for promotional purposes.

columns.name: PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT
columns.description: Type: categorical string. Use: Final segmentation classification for physicians based on prescribing behavior, engagement patterns, and business potential during the reporting month. Critical for physician targeting, campaign personalization, and performance analysis across different physician groups.

columns.name: PHYSICIAN_TIER
columns.description: This column indicates prioritization system for physicians based on prescribing potential, market influence, and strategic importance. Tiers typically range from 1 (highest priority) to 3 (standard priority) with 'No Tier' indicating unclassified physicians.

columns.name: PRIMARY_SPECIALTY
columns.description: This column indicates Physician's primary medical specialty (e.g., Cardiology, Nephrology, Internal Medicine).

columns.name: PRIMARY_SPECIALTY_GROUP
columns.description: This column indicates Aggregated specialty classification for higher-level analysis and targeting (e.g., PCP for Primary Care Physicians, CARD for Cardiology, NEPH for Nephrology).

columns.name: REGION_NAME
columns.description: This column indicates Highest level of geographic organizational structure for executive reporting and strategic market analysis. Enables regional performance measurement and supports high-level market strategy development.

columns.name: RELEVATE_CARDIZOR_POC_RULE_1_728X90_BA1
columns.description: This column indicates Count of impressions or engagements for Cardizor from Relevate Health POC Rule 1 creative (728×90 banner, BA1 variant) during the reporting month. Relevate Health is a digital advertising platform specializing in healthcare professional targeting.

columns.name: RELEVATE_CARDIZOR_POC_RULE_1_728X90_BA2
columns.description: This column indicates Count of clicks or engagements from Relevate Health POC Rule 1 creative (728×90 banner, BA2 variant) for Cardizor during the reporting month. Relevate Health is a digital advertising platform specializing in healthcare professional targeting.

columns.name: RELEVATE_CARDIZOR_POC_RULE_2_728X90_BA1
columns.description: This column indicates Count of impressions or engagements from Relevate Health POC Rule 2 creative (728×90 banner, BA1 variant) for Cardizor during the reporting month.  Critical for measuring display advertising reach and frequency through healthcare-focused media channels.

columns.name: RELEVATE_CARDIZOR_POC_RULE_2_728X90_BA2
columns.description: This column indicates Count of clicks or engagements from Relevate Health POC Rule 2 creative (728×90 banner, BA2 variant) for Cardizor during the reporting month.  Critical for measuring display advertising engagement and click-through rates through healthcare-focused media channels.

columns.name: RELEVATE_CARDIZOR_POC_RULE_3_728X90_BA1
columns.description: This column indicates Count of impressions or engagements from Relevate Health POC Rule 3 creative (728×90 banner, BA1 variant) for Cardizor during the reporting month.  Critical for measuring display advertising reach and frequency through healthcare-focused media channels.

columns.name: RELEVATE_CARDIZOR_POC_RULE_3_728X90_BA2
columns.description: This column indicates Count of clicks or engagements from Relevate Health POC Rule 3 creative (728×90 banner, BA2 variant) for Cardizor during the reporting month.  Critical for measuring display advertising engagement and click-through rates through healthcare-focused media channels.

columns.name: RELEVATE_HEALTH_CLICKS
columns.description: This column indicates Aggregate count of Relevate Health advertising clicks generated by physicians during the reporting month.  Critical for measuring display advertising engagement and calculating click-through rates.

columns.name: RELEVATE_HEALTH_IMPRESSIONS
columns.description: This column indicates Aggregate count of Relevate Health advertising impressions delivered to physicians during the reporting month.  Critical for measuring display advertising reach and frequency through healthcare-focused media channels.

columns.name: SAMPLES_SHIP_QUANTITY
columns.description: This column indicates Actual quantity of pharmaceutical samples shipped to physicians during the reporting month. Sample shipments represent the physical distribution of trial medications to physicians for patient evaluation. Critical for measuring sample program execution and reconciling with modeled sample counts.

columns.name: SECONDARY_SPECIALTY
columns.description: This column indicates Additional specialty classification for physicians with multiple areas of practice. Provides granular targeting opportunities for therapeutic areas and supports comprehensive physician profiling. Enables identification of physicians with dual specialties for cross-therapeutic area promotional strategies.

columns.name: SPEAKER_ATTENDEES_CARDIZOR
columns.description: This column indicates Count of attendees in brand-specific speaker programs, Cardizor during the reporting month. Brand-specific speaker programs focus exclusively on the target pharmaceutical product.

columns.name: SPEAKER_ATTENDEES_DUAL
columns.description: This column indicates Count of attendees in dual-topic speaker programs during the reporting month. Dual-topic programs cover multiple therapeutic areas or products in a single educational session. Critical for measuring multi-product educational program reach and cross-therapeutic area physician engagement.

columns.name: STATE
columns.description: Practice State of HCPs or Physician. Two-character practice state code for the physician,  indicates the state associated with the practice location for targeting and reporting.

columns.name: TERRITORY_NAME
columns.description: This column indicates Sales representative territory designation for field force performance analysis, territory optimization, and sales management reporting. Enables territory-level performance measurement and supports sales force planning and compensation analysis.

columns.name: TOTAL_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the comprehensive count of all sales representative calls made to physicians during the reporting month, including face-to-face, virtual, and other call types. Represents the total volume of personal promotional activities and is a key metric for measuring sales force engagement and physician relationship building.

columns.name: TOTAL_DEEPINTENT_ENGAGEMENTS
columns.description: This column indicates comprehensive count of all physician engagements with DeepIntent digital advertising campaigns during the reporting month. DeepIntent is advertising platform that enables targeted physician engagement. Includes impressions, clicks, and other engagement metrics across multiple campaign IDs. Critical for measuring healthcare-specific programmatic advertising effectiveness.

columns.name: TOTAL_DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS
columns.description: This column indicates the master roll-up metric representing total digital promotional engagements across all digital marketing channels during the reporting month. Includes engagements from DeepIntent, Relevate Health, DMD, Epocrates, Medscape, and Veeva platforms. Provides comprehensive view of overall digital promotional pressure and physician engagement across all digital touchpoints. Critical for measuring total digital marketing effectiveness and physician digital engagement patterns.

columns.name: TOTAL_DMD_EMAILS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of emails sent through the DMD (Digital Marketing Database) platform during the reporting month. DMD is a specialized digital marketing platform that enables targeted physician communication. Critical for measuring DMD-specific campaign performance and physician engagement through this channel.

columns.name: TOTAL_EMAILS
columns.description: This column indicates the comprehensive count of all promotional emails sent to physicians across all digital marketing platforms during the reporting month. Includes emails from various channels such as DMD, Veeva, and other email marketing systems. Critical metric for measuring digital promotional reach and engagement.

columns.name: TOTAL_EPOCRATES_ENGAGEMENTS
columns.description: This column indicates the comprehensive count of all physician engagements with Epocrates platform content during the reporting month. Includes interactions with DocAlerts, home screen messages, monographs, and display advertisements Critical for measuring digital engagement through medical reference platforms.

columns.name: TOTAL_MEDSCAPE_ENGAGEMENTS
columns.description: This column indicates comprehensive count of all physician engagements with Medscape platform content during the reporting month. Includes interactions with email campaigns, quiz participation, monograph views, and other educational content. Critical for measuring medical education platform engagement and physician learning interactions.

columns.name: TOTAL_RELEVATE_ENGAGEMENTS
columns.description: This column indicates comprehensive count of all physician engagements with Relevate Health digital advertising campaigns during the reporting month. Includes impressions, clicks, and other engagement metrics from Relevate Health's programmatic advertising platform. Critical for measuring programmatic advertising effectiveness and physician engagement through digital media.

columns.name: TOTAL_SAMPLES_COUNT
columns.description: This column inidicates the comprehensive count of samples distributed to physicians during the reporting month across all sample programs and channels. Critical metric for measuring sample program effectiveness and physician engagement.

columns.name: TOTAL_SPEAKER
columns.description: This column inidicates the comprehensive count of speaker program engagements and attendees attributable to the physician during the reporting month. Includes both physician participation as speakers and attendance at speaker events. Critical metric for measuring key opinion leader (KOL) engagement and educational program effectiveness.

columns.name: TOTAL_SPEAKER_ATTENDEES
columns.description: This column indicates Total count of attendees attributable to physicians across all speaker programs during the reporting month. Speaker programs are educational events where key opinion leaders present clinical information to other physicians.

columns.name: TOTAL_VEEVA_EMAIL_CLICKS
columns.description: This column indicates Count of all Veeva email link clicks (including multiple clicks from same physician) during the reporting month. Veeva is a CRM platform used by pharmaceutical sales representatives for physician communication. Critical for measuring total email engagement volume and calculating overall click-through rates.

columns.name: TOTAL_VEEVA_EMAIL_OPENS
columns.description: This column indicates Count of all Veeva email opens (including multiple opens from same physician) during the reporting month. Veeva is a CRM platform used by pharmaceutical sales representatives for physician communication. Critical for measuring total email engagement volume and calculating overall open rates.

columns.name: VEEVA_EMAIL_CLICKS
columns.description: This column indicates Count of unique physicians who clicked at least one link in Veeva email communications during the reporting month. Veeva is a CRM platform used by pharmaceutical sales representatives for physician communication. Critical for measuring sales rep email engagement effectiveness and calculating unique click-through rates.

columns.name: VEEVA_EMAIL_DELIVERED
columns.description: This column indicates Count of Veeva emails successfully delivered to physicians during the reporting month. Veeva is a CRM platform used by pharmaceutical sales representatives for physician communication. Critical for measuring sales rep email campaign reach and delivery rates. Important for campaign performance analysis and list quality assessment.

columns.name: VEEVA_EMAIL_OPENS
columns.description: This column indicates Count of unique physicians who opened Veeva email communications during the reporting month. Veeva is a CRM platform used by pharmaceutical sales representatives for physician communication. Critical for measuring sales rep email engagement and calculating unique open rates.

columns.name: VIRTUAL_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of virtual sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month, including video calls, phone calls, and other remote communication methods. Virtual calls enable efficient physician engagement while maintaining personal connection, especially important for geographically dispersed territories or during travel restrictions. Critical for measuring remote physician engagement and digital sales force capabilities.

columns.name: VIRTUAL_P1_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of virtual Priority-1 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Represents remote engagement for the most important physicians, enabling efficient high-priority physician interaction. Critical for measuring virtual engagement with high-value targets and digital sales force effectiveness. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: VIRTUAL_P2_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of virtual Priority-2 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Represents remote engagement for medium-priority physicians, balancing efficiency with relationship building. Critical for measuring virtual engagement with standard targets and digital sales force capabilities. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: VIRTUAL_P3_CALLS
columns.description: This column indicates the count of virtual Priority-3 sales calls made to physicians during the reporting month. Represents remote engagement for standard-priority physicians, typically for routine follow-up or efficient coverage. Critical for measuring comprehensive virtual physician coverage and digital sales force efficiency. Whenever user mentions the call position, we should be using this column for the calculation.

columns.name: ZIP_CODE

sample_queries.user_input: Are there outliers or null values in the speaker program exposure data for Q3?
sample_queries.query:
WITH q3_data AS (
    SELECT
        "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT" AS physician_segment,
        "MONTH_YEAR" AS month_year,
        "TOTAL_SPEAKER" AS total_speaker,
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR")::INT AS year,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR")::INT AS month
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR") IN (7, 8, 9)
),
stats AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(total_speaker) AS avg_total_speaker,
        STDDEV(total_speaker) AS stddev_total_speaker
    FROM q3_data
    WHERE total_speaker IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    qd.*
FROM q3_data AS qd
CROSS JOIN stats AS s
WHERE qd.total_speaker IS NULL
   OR qd.total_speaker > s.avg_total_speaker + (3 * s.stddev_total_speaker)
   OR qd.total_speaker < s.avg_total_speaker - (3 * s.stddev_total_speaker);
sample_queries.description:
When a user asks:
"Are there outliers or null values in the speaker program exposure data for Q3?",
the system should interpret it as:

Metric objective
The goal is to detect data quality issues—specifically null values and statistical outliers—in Q3 speaker‑program exposure counts (TOTAL_SPEAKER) across physician segments and months. Q3 is defined as months 7–9 (July–September) of any year.
​

Data subset for Q3
Use "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset" as the source.

In CTE q3_data, select:

"PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT" as physician_segment.

"MONTH_YEAR" as month_year.

"TOTAL_SPEAKER" as total_speaker.

Extracted year and month components for reference using EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") and EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR").

Filter rows to Q3 months with EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR") IN (7, 8, 9), ensuring only Q3 exposure records are analyzed.
​

Outlier and null detection logic
In CTE stats, compute summary statistics from non‑null Q3 records:

avg_total_speaker = AVG(total_speaker).

stddev_total_speaker = STDDEV(total_speaker).

In the final SELECT, join every Q3 row to these statistics via CROSS JOIN stats s and flag rows where:

total_speaker IS NULL, capturing missing exposure values.

total_speaker > avg_total_speaker + 3 * stddev_total_speaker, indicating high outliers more than 3 standard deviations above the Q3 mean.

total_speaker < avg_total_speaker - 3 * stddev_total_speaker, indicating low outliers more than 3 standard deviations below the mean.
​

SELECT DISTINCT qd.* returns each unique Q3 record that violates these rules, listing physician segment, month, exposure count, year, and month.

Interpretation of the result
Any rows returned represent potential outliers or null data points in speaker‑program exposure for Q3 that may require investigation or cleaning before further analysis.

If the query returns no rows, it implies that all Q3 TOTAL_SPEAKER values are non‑null and fall within the mean ± 3 standard deviations range, suggesting no extreme anomalies under this statistical rule.
​

sample_queries.user_input: Is there a mismatch in HCP IDs between sales and promo activity datasets?
sample_queries.query:
WITH filtered AS (
    SELECT
        "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
        SUM("CARDIZOR_TRX") AS total_trx,
        SUM("TOTAL_CALLS") AS total_calls,
        SUM("TOTAL_SAMPLES_COUNT") AS total_samples,
        SUM("TOTAL_EMAILS") AS total_emails,
        SUM("TOTAL_SPEAKER") AS total_speaker,
        SUM("TOTAL_DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS") AS total_digital
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE LEFT("MONTH_YEAR"::text, 4) = '2025'
    GROUP BY "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
)
SELECT
    "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
    'sales_only' AS mismatch_type
FROM filtered
WHERE total_trx > 0
    AND total_calls = 0
    AND total_samples = 0
    AND total_emails = 0
    AND total_speaker = 0
    AND total_digital = 0

UNION ALL

SELECT
    "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
    'activities_only' AS mismatch_type
FROM filtered
WHERE total_trx = 0
    AND (
        total_calls > 0
        OR total_samples > 0
        OR total_emails > 0
        OR total_speaker > 0
        OR total_digital > 0
    );
sample_queries.description:
When a user asks:
"Is there a mismatch in HCP IDs between sales and promo activity datasets?",
the system should interpret it as:

Metric objective
The aim is to detect HCP‑level mismatches between sales (Cardizor TRx) and promotional activity within a single integrated dataset for a given year (2025). Specifically, the query identifies HCPs who appear with sales but no tracked promo activity, and those with promo activity but no recorded sales.
​

Data preparation and aggregation
Use "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset" as the underlying table containing both sales and promotional KPIs by HCP and month.

In CTE filtered, restrict to records from calendar year 2025 via WHERE LEFT("MONTH_YEAR"::text, 4) = '2025'.
​

Group by "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID" and aggregate annual totals per HCP:

total_trx = SUM("CARDIZOR_TRX").

total_calls = SUM("TOTAL_CALLS").

total_samples = SUM("TOTAL_SAMPLES_COUNT").

total_emails = SUM("TOTAL_EMAILS").

total_speaker = SUM("TOTAL_SPEAKER").

total_digital = SUM("TOTAL_DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS").

This produces one row per HCP with consolidated 2025 sales and promo counts.
​

Mismatch conditions
The final query returns two types of mismatches via UNION ALL:

Sales only (no activities)

Criteria:

total_trx > 0 (HCP generated Cardizor TRx).

All promo metrics are zero: total_calls = 0, total_samples = 0, total_emails = 0, total_speaker = 0, total_digital = 0.

These HCPs are labeled 'sales_only' in mismatch_type, indicating sales without recorded promotional touchpoints.

Activities only (no sales)

Criteria:

total_trx = 0.

At least one promo metric is positive: total_calls > 0 OR total_samples > 0 OR total_emails > 0 OR total_speaker > 0 OR total_digital > 0.

These HCPs are labeled 'activities_only', indicating promotional engagement without corresponding Cardizor TRx.

Interpretation of results
Each returned row contains "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID" and mismatch_type, clearly signaling where HCP IDs show asymmetry between sales and promotional activity.

The presence and count of these records quantify the degree of mismatch between sales and promo datasets and highlight HCPs that may need data reconciliation or strategic follow‑up (e.g., high activity but no sales, or sales occurring without observed promo support).
​

sample_queries.user_input: Do digital promotions show a consistent seasonal pattern across years? Are there spikes during specific quarters or events?
sample_queries.query:
WITH monthly_data AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") AS year,
        EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR") AS month,
        CASE 
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR") IN (1, 2, 3) THEN 'q1'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR") IN (4, 5, 6) THEN 'q2'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR") IN (7, 8, 9) THEN 'q3'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR") IN (10, 11, 12) THEN 'q4'
        END AS quarter,
        SUM("TOTAL_DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS") AS total_total_digital_promotions
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR"), EXTRACT(MONTH FROM "MONTH_YEAR")
),
yearly_stats AS (
    SELECT
        year,
        AVG(total_total_digital_promotions * 1.0) AS avg_promotions,
        STDDEV(total_total_digital_promotions * 1.0) AS stddev_promotions
    FROM monthly_data
    GROUP BY year
)
SELECT
    m.year,
    m.month,
    m.quarter,
    m.total_total_digital_promotions,
    ROUND(
        m.total_total_digital_promotions * 100.0 / SUM(m.total_total_digital_promotions) OVER (PARTITION BY m.year),
        2
    ) AS pct_of_year,
    CASE
        WHEN m.total_total_digital_promotions > (y.avg_promotions + y.stddev_promotions) 
        THEN 'spike'
        ELSE 'normal'
    END AS spike_flag
FROM monthly_data m
JOIN yearly_stats y
    ON m.year = y.year
ORDER BY m.year, m.month;

When a user asks:

the system should interpret it as:

The user wants to examine monthly and quarterly patterns in total digital promotions over multiple years, quantify each month’s contribution to its year’s total, and flag statistically significant spikes (months where digital activity is notably higher than that year’s typical level).
​

Derived monthly metrics (monthly_data CTE):

stddev_promotions: standard deviation of monthly promotions for each year.

Business questions:

sample_queries.user_input: How many HCP with >10% TRx growth have <5 rep call exposure? What % of total modeling universe is this?
sample_queries.query:
WITH p1 AS (
    SELECT "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID", SUM("CARDIZOR_TRX") AS trx_p1
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") = 2024
    GROUP BY "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
),
p2 AS (
    SELECT "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID", SUM("CARDIZOR_TRX") AS trx_p2, SUM("TOTAL_CALLS") AS calls_p2
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") = 2025
    GROUP BY "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
),
growth_calc AS (
    SELECT
        p2."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
        p1.trx_p1,
        p2.trx_p2,
        p2.calls_p2,
        CASE WHEN p1.trx_p1 > 0
             THEN ((p2.trx_p2 - p1.trx_p1) * 100.0) / p1.trx_p1
             ELSE NULL
        END AS trx_growth_pct
    FROM p2
    LEFT JOIN p1
      ON p2."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID" = p1."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
),
universe AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID") AS total_hcps
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS hcp_count,
    ROUND(
        COUNT(*) * 100.0 /
        (SELECT total_hcps FROM universe),
        2
    ) AS pct_of_universe
FROM growth_calc
WHERE trx_growth_pct > 10
  AND calls_p2 < 5;
sample_queries.description:
When a user asks:
"How many HCP with >10% TRx growth have <5 rep call exposure? What % of total modeling universe is this?",
the system should interpret it as:

Metric objective
The query quantifies HCPs who show strong year‑over‑year TRx growth for Cardizor (>10% from 2024 to 2025) despite having low sales‑rep call exposure (<5 total calls in 2025), and then expresses this cohort as a percentage of the total HCP universe used for modeling.
​

Period definitions and TRx growth calculation
Use "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset" as the source.

p1 aggregates 2024 performance per HCP:

For each "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID", compute trx_p1 = SUM("CARDIZOR_TRX") where EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") = 2024.

p2 aggregates 2025 performance per HCP:

trx_p2 = SUM("CARDIZOR_TRX"), calls_p2 = SUM("TOTAL_CALLS") for records where year = 2025.
​

growth_calc left‑joins p2 to p1 on HCP ID and calculates TRx growth percentage:

If trx_p1 > 0, trx_growth_pct = ((trx_p2 - trx_p1) * 100.0) / trx_p1.

If trx_p1 = 0, growth is set to NULL to avoid division by zero and to ignore HCPs without a 2024 baseline.

Universe size and cohort selection
universe computes the modeling universe as COUNT(DISTINCT "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID") over the entire dataset, representing all HCPs with any record in the table, regardless of year.
​

The final SELECT filters growth_calc to the desired cohort:

trx_growth_pct > 10: HCPs with more than 10% Cardizor TRx growth from 2024 to 2025.

calls_p2 < 5: HCPs with fewer than 5 total rep calls in 2025 (low call exposure).

Output metrics
COUNT(*) AS hcp_count: number of HCPs in this high‑growth, low‑call cohort.

pct_of_universe: the share of the total HCP modeling universe that this cohort represents, computed as:

ROUND(COUNT(*) * 100.0 / (SELECT total_hcps FROM universe), 2).

This directly answers both parts of the question: the absolute count of such HCPs and their percentage of the overall universe, enabling assessment of missed engagement opportunities where growth occurred despite limited rep activity.

sample_queries.user_input: Which segment sees high non personal engagement but low personal engagement?
sample_queries.query:
WITH engagement AS (
    SELECT
        "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
        AVG("TOTAL_CALLS"::FLOAT) AS avg_calls,
        AVG("TOTAL_SAMPLES_COUNT"::FLOAT) AS avg_samples,
        AVG("TOTAL_EMAILS"::FLOAT) AS avg_emails,
        AVG("TOTAL_DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS"::FLOAT) AS avg_digital_promotions,
        SUM(COALESCE("TOTAL_CALLS", 0)) AS calls,
        SUM(COALESCE("TOTAL_SAMPLES_COUNT", 0)) AS samples,
        SUM(COALESCE("TOTAL_EMAILS", 0)) AS emails,
        SUM(COALESCE("TOTAL_DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS", 0)) AS digital_promotions
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") = 2025
    GROUP BY "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT"
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
        (avg_calls + avg_samples) AS personal_score,
        (avg_emails + avg_digital_promotions) AS non_personal_score,
        calls, samples, emails, digital_promotions
    FROM engagement
)
SELECT
    "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
    calls, samples, emails, digital_promotions
FROM ranked
WHERE non_personal_score > (SELECT AVG(non_personal_score) FROM ranked)
  AND personal_score     < (SELECT AVG(personal_score)     FROM ranked);

sample_queries.query:
WITH region_name_summary AS (
    SELECT
        "REGION_NAME",
        COUNT(DISTINCT "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID") AS hcp_count,
        AVG("TOTAL_CALLS" + "TOTAL_SAMPLES_COUNT") AS avg_personal_engagement,
        AVG("TOTAL_EMAILS" + "TOTAL_DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS") AS avg_non_personal_engagement
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") = 2025
    GROUP BY "REGION_NAME"
),
percentiles AS (
    SELECT
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.75) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY hcp_count) AS hcp_p75,
        PERCENTILE_CONT(0.25) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (avg_personal_engagement + avg_non_personal_engagement)) AS engagement_p25
    FROM region_name_summary
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        rs.*,
        CASE
            WHEN rs.hcp_count > p.hcp_p75
            THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS hcp_density_flag,
        CASE
            WHEN (rs.avg_personal_engagement + rs.avg_non_personal_engagement) < p.engagement_p25
            THEN 'low' ELSE 'high' END AS engagement_flag
    FROM region_name_summary AS rs
    CROSS JOIN percentiles AS p
)
SELECT
    "REGION_NAME",
    hcp_count,
    avg_personal_engagement,
    avg_non_personal_engagement
FROM ranked
WHERE hcp_density_flag = 'high'
  AND engagement_flag = 'low'
ORDER BY hcp_count DESC;

sample_queries.user_input: Which HCP segments had increased call frequency but stagnant or declining TRx?
sample_queries.query:
WITH p1 AS (
    SELECT
        "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
        "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
        SUM(COALESCE("TOTAL_CALLS", 0)) AS calls_p1,
        SUM(COALESCE("CARDIZOR_TRX", 0)) AS trx_p1
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") = 2024
    GROUP BY "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT", "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
),
p2 AS (
    SELECT
        "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
        "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
        SUM(COALESCE("TOTAL_CALLS", 0)) AS calls_p2,
        SUM(COALESCE("CARDIZOR_TRX", 0)) AS trx_p2
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") = 2025
    GROUP BY "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT", "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
),
growth AS (
    SELECT
        p2."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
        p2."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
        p1.calls_p1,
        p2.calls_p2,
        p1.trx_p1,
        p2.trx_p2,
        CASE 
            WHEN p1.calls_p1 > 0 
            THEN ((p2.calls_p2 - p1.calls_p1) * 100.0) / p1.calls_p1
            ELSE NULL 
        END AS calls_growth_pct,
        CASE 
            WHEN p1.trx_p1 > 0 
            THEN ((p2.trx_p2 - p1.trx_p1) * 100.0) / p1.trx_p1
            ELSE NULL 
        END AS trx_growth_pct
    FROM p2
    LEFT JOIN p1
      ON p2."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT" = p1."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT"
     AND p2."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID" = p1."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
)
SELECT
    "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
    COUNT(DISTINCT "PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID") AS hcp_count,
    AVG(calls_growth_pct::FLOAT) AS avg_call_growth_pct,
    AVG(trx_growth_pct::FLOAT) AS avg_trx_growth_pct
FROM growth
WHERE calls_growth_pct > 0
  AND (trx_growth_pct <= 0 OR trx_growth_pct IS NULL)
GROUP BY "PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT"
ORDER BY avg_call_growth_pct DESC;

The query finds HCP segments where average call volume increases year‑over‑year from 2024 to 2025, but Cardizor TRx are flat or declining, and then summarizes those segments.

How call and TRx growth are measured
p1 (2024) and p2 (2025) aggregate by PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT and PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID:

calls_p1 / calls_p2: total calls per HCP per year.

trx_p1 / trx_p2: total Cardizor TRx per HCP per year.

growth computes, per HCP:

calls_growth_pct = percentage change in calls from 2024 to 2025, if 2024 calls_p1 > 0.

trx_growth_pct = percentage change in TRx from 2024 to 2025, if 2024 trx_p1 > 0.

Selecting segments with increased calls but stagnant/declining TRx
Final SELECT groups growth by PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT, but only for HCPs where:

calls_growth_pct > 0 (calls increased).

trx_growth_pct ≤ 0 or NULL (TRx did not grow or data missing).

For each qualifying segment, it returns:

hcp_count: distinct HCPs in that situation.

avg_call_growth_pct: average call growth.

avg_trx_growth_pct: average TRx growth (≤ 0).

Ordered by avg_call_growth_pct descending, the output highlights which HCP segments received more calls without corresponding TRx gains, indicating inefficient promotional effort.

WITH latest AS (

    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
),
bounds AS (

        DATE_TRUNC('quarter', max_data_date) - INTERVAL '6 months' AS previous_quarter_start

),
p_last AS (
    SELECT
        s."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
        s."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
        SUM(COALESCE(s."TOTAL_CALLS", 0))  AS calls_last,
        SUM(COALESCE(s."CARDIZOR_TRX", 0)) AS trx_last
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset" s
    CROSS JOIN bounds b
    WHERE s."MONTH_YEAR" >= b.last_quarter_start
      AND s."MONTH_YEAR" <  b.current_quarter_start
    GROUP BY s."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT", s."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
),
p_prev AS (
    SELECT
        s."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT",
        s."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",
        SUM(COALESCE(s."TOTAL_CALLS", 0))  AS calls_prev,
        SUM(COALESCE(s."CARDIZOR_TRX", 0)) AS trx_prev
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset" s
    CROSS JOIN bounds b
    WHERE s."MONTH_YEAR" >= b.previous_quarter_start
      AND s."MONTH_YEAR" <  b.last_quarter_start
    GROUP BY s."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT", s."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID"
),
growth AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(pl."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT", pp."PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT") AS physician_segment,
        COALESCE(pl."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID",  pp."PHYSICIAN_NPI_ID")  AS physician_npi_id,

        pl.calls_last,
        pp.trx_prev,
        pl.trx_last,

sample_queries.user_input: How did the overall promotion mix across all channels change in 2025 compared to 2024?

WITH YearlyPromotionMetrics AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") AS PromotionYear,
        SUM("TOTAL_CALLS")                  AS TotalCalls,
        SUM("TOTAL_SAMPLES_COUNT")          AS TotalSamples,
        SUM("TOTAL_SPEAKER")                AS TotalSpeakerPrograms,
        SUM("TOTAL_EMAILS")                 AS TotalEmails,
        SUM("TOTAL_DMD_EMAILS")             AS TotalDMDEmails,
        SUM("TOTAL_EPOCRATES_ENGAGEMENTS")  AS TotalEpocratesEngagements,
        SUM("TOTAL_RELEVATE_ENGAGEMENTS")   AS TotalRelevateEngagements,
        SUM("TOTAL_DEEPINTENT_ENGAGEMENTS") AS TotalDeepIntentEngagements,
        SUM("TOTAL_MEDSCAPE_ENGAGEMENTS")   AS TotalMedscapeEngagements,
        SUM("TOTAL_DIGITAL_PROMOTIONS")     AS TotalDigitalPromotions
    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"
    WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR") IN (2024, 2025)
    GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR")
),
PromotionsComparison AS (
    SELECT
        P2024.TotalCalls                 AS TotalCalls_2024,
        P2025.TotalCalls                 AS TotalCalls_2025,
        P2024.TotalSamples               AS TotalSamples_2024,
        P2025.TotalSamples               AS TotalSamples_2025,
        P2024.TotalSpeakerPrograms       AS TotalSpeakerPrograms_2024,
        P2025.TotalSpeakerPrograms       AS TotalSpeakerPrograms_2025,
        P2024.TotalEmails                AS TotalEmails_2024,
        P2025.TotalEmails                AS TotalEmails_2025,
        P2024.TotalDMDEmails             AS TotalDMDEmails_2024,
        P2025.TotalDMDEmails             AS TotalDMDEmails_2025,
        P2024.TotalEpocratesEngagements  AS TotalEpocratesEngagements_2024,
        P2025.TotalEpocratesEngagements  AS TotalEpocratesEngagements_2025,
        P2024.TotalRelevateEngagements   AS TotalRelevateEngagements_2024,
        P2025.TotalRelevateEngagements   AS TotalRelevateEngagements_2025,
        P2024.TotalDeepIntentEngagements AS TotalDeepIntentEngagements_2024,
        P2025.TotalDeepIntentEngagements AS TotalDeepIntentEngagements_2025,
        P2024.TotalMedscapeEngagements   AS TotalMedscapeEngagements_2024,
        P2025.TotalMedscapeEngagements   AS TotalMedscapeEngagements_2025,
        P2024.TotalDigitalPromotions     AS TotalDigitalPromotions_2024,
        P2025.TotalDigitalPromotions     AS TotalDigitalPromotions_2025
    FROM YearlyPromotionMetrics P2024
    JOIN YearlyPromotionMetrics P2025
      ON P2024.PromotionYear = 2024
     AND P2025.PromotionYear = 2025
)
SELECT
    Metric,
    Total_in_2024,
    Total_in_2025,
    ROUND((Total_in_2025 - Total_in_2024) * 100.0 / NULLIF(Total_in_2024, 0), 2) AS PercentageChange
FROM PromotionsComparison pc,

        ('Total Medscape Engagements',   pc.TotalMedscapeEngagements_2024,  pc.TotalMedscapeEngagements_2025),
        ('Total Digital Promotions',     pc.TotalDigitalPromotions_2024,    pc.TotalDigitalPromotions_2025)
) AS Metrics(Metric, Total_in_2024, Total_in_2025)

    "TotalCalls_2025",
    "CardizorTRx_2024",
    "CardizorTRx_2025"

"CardizorTRx_2024" and "CardizorTRx_2025":

"TotalCalls_2025" > "TotalCalls_2024": call volume increased from 2024 to 2025.

For each qualifying segment the query returns:

"PHYSICIAN_SEGMENT" (uppercased name).

TotalCalls_2024, TotalCalls_2025.

CardizorTRx_2024, CardizorTRx_2025.

sample_queries.query:
WITH YearlySales AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR")::INT AS SalesYear,

    FROM "mmm"."Segmentation_Master_Dataset"

    GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM "MONTH_YEAR")::INT
),
IncrementalSales AS (
    SELECT
        SalesYear,
        TotalCardizorTRX,
        LAG(TotalCardizorTRX, 1, 0) OVER (ORDER BY SalesYear) AS PreviousYearTRX
    FROM YearlySales
)
